items.raw_excerpt: Owners of a café and pastry shop in Keflavík say four Israeli tourists threatened an employee and attempted to damage the premises after noticing a map of Palestine displayed on a wall. Palestine-born Farah Al-Qasem, who runs Lava Sweets on Hafnargata with her husband, Diyaa Atatri, said the men entered shortly after the business opened…
items.summary_en: Four Israeli tourists came to a cafe in Keflavik and saw a map of Palestine on the wall. They shouted at a worker and tried to damage the store. The cafe owner, Farah Al-Qasem, said the men left after staff asked them to go.

items.raw_excerpt: El futbolista ya recibió un homenaje la pasada semana en la localidad, un acto multitudinario al que acudieron cerca de 7.000 personas. Más información: Ferran Torres se da un baño de masas en Foios, su pueblo natal: "Sentía que iba a ser el protagonista de la final"
items.summary_en: Ferran Torres now has a mural in Foios, a small village in Valencia where he was born. The football star recently joined Paris Saint-Germain and helped win the World Cup. Last week, nearly 7,000 people came to a tribute for him in the village.
